QF.id: Retirement Planning Products: National Pension System (NPS)_48

question.text: Under the old tax regime, what is the maximum deduction available under Section 80CCD(1) for a salaried employee's own NPS contribution (as stated in the NISM Series XVII Retirement Adviser workbook, p. 144)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the old tax regime, Section 80CCD(1) caps a salaried employee's own NPS contribution deduction at 10% of Basic + DA, within the overall Rs. 1.5 lakh Section 80C ceiling (NISM Series XVII workbook p. 144). The Trap: Option B (14% of Basic + DA) is the figure the workbook cites for the new tax regime treatment on the same page, which is why the audit flagged the original stem as ambiguous on the regime question. 14% is also the cap for employer contribution under 80CCD(2) for Central Government employees. Option C (20% of gross income) applies to non-salaried (self-employed) individuals, not salaried. Option D (Rs. 1.5 lakh) is the umbrella Section 80C ceiling, not the 80CCD(1) sub-limit. Note: The original stem did not specify the tax regime, and p. 144 references both a 10% old-regime figure and a 14% new-regime figure. The stem now explicitly anchors the question to the old tax regime, making option A uniquely correct.
